title: Pilgrimage: Sarnath
hookLine: the Deer Park where the first sermon was given

lines: FIVE OLD FRIENDS MAKE A PACT.
cards: Five men are sitting in a park near the city of Benares when they see someone walking toward them on the road. They know him. He used to fast and strain alongside them, and then he quit and started eating again.
They decided he'd gone soft. So they make a pact: when he gets here, nobody stands up. Nobody takes his bowl.
Maybe offer him a seat, if he insists. Then he comes closer, and something about the way he walks undoes the whole plan. One takes his robe.
Another sets out water. Someone offers a seat. The park was full of deer, and the talk he gave there is why pilgrims still come.

teach.b: First, the place. The texts call it Isipatana, the deer park near Benares. Today it's Sarnath, a quiet green with the ruins of old monasteries and a great round stupa of brick and stone.
Pilgrims walk around it; some sit on the grass and listen to the teaching read aloud. Second, the talk, called Setting in Motion the Wheel of the Teaching.

It opens not with doctrine but with a warning about two dead ends: chasing pleasure, and punishing the body. The Buddha had tried both. Between them, he says, is a middle way, and it leads to peace and to awakening.
Third, the four truths. There is suffering. It has a cause, the craving that keeps reaching for more.
It can end. And there is a path to its ending. Here's the detail worth keeping: in the discourse, each truth comes with a job.
Suffering is to be understood. Craving is to be let go. The ending is to be realized.
The path is to be walked.
Not four statements to agree with: four tasks. Fourth, the moment it lands. As the Buddha speaks, one of the five, Kondanna, sees it for himself: whatever arises also passes away.
The Buddha says, Kondanna has understood.
And the text says the gods shout the news from one heaven to the next: at Benares, in the deer park, the wheel has been set rolling.

how: Pilgrims visit Sarnath near Varanasi to walk around the great stupa, see the ruins of ancient monasteries, and chant or listen to the discourse on setting the wheel of the teaching in motion.

o: a journey to the places of the Buddha's life
a holiday spent touring old ruins and parks
a long fast taken to punish the body

s: the Buddha's first listeners at the deer park welcomed him gladly from the start
the five had agreed not to stand up for him. when he came near, they stood anyway.
in the discourse, each of the four truths comes with a task
suffering understood, craving let go, the ending realized, the path walked.
the talk begins with the middle way between two extremes
it warns against chasing pleasure and punishing the body before it gives the four truths.

games.q: you're one of the five. your old companion, who gave up the hard fasting, is walking toward you. you agreed not to stand. what do you do?
o: keep your pact and stay seated.
get up, take his robe and set out water.
games.why: the pact fell apart. as he came near, they got up, took his bowl and robe, and set out a seat and water.

practice: Breathe out, then say the four truths quietly, one per breath: there is suffering, there is a cause of suffering, there is an end of suffering, there is a path.
Say them again with each task under your breath: understand, let go, realize, walk. Then let the words go and breathe, on the grass with the deer.

wordCard.voice: Pilgrimage. The road to the holy places. Its third stop is Sarnath, the deer park where the Buddha set the wheel of the teaching rolling. Today's word.

orig.note: Pali dhammacakka: the wheel of the teaching, set rolling at the deer park.

carryVoice: Your line: where he taught. Four truths, and each one a task. I'll be here tomorrow.
